HL1.citation: Hamilton-Lisle gr-qc/0411060v2 (31 Aug 2006), local sources/gr-qc_0411060.pdf, p.1, section I, equation (1)
HL1.quoted: ds^2 = -dt_ff^2 + (dr + beta dt_ff)^2 + r^2 (dtheta^2 + sin^2 theta dphi^2)
HL1.conditions: Schwarzschild river; beta is inward speed in light-speed units; t_ff is proper time of radial infall from rest at infinity. Overall factor 1.

HL2.citation: Hamilton-Lisle, same local copy, p.1, section I, equation (2)
HL2.conditions: Spherical Schwarzschild mass M; beta in light-speed units. G M here is an oracle parameter, not S9b's orbital GM.

HL4.citation: Hamilton-Lisle, same local copy, p.3, section II.A, equation (4)
HL4.conditions: Spherical mass-function metric (3); units c = G = 1. M(r) is live, not assumed constant.

V4.citation: Visser gr-qc/9712010v2 (15 Dec 1997), local sources/gr-qc_9712010.pdf, pp.3-4, equation (4)
V4.conditions: I is the 3 by 3 identity; barotropic, inviscid fluid and irrotational flow; scalar acoustic velocity potential; Newtonian flat physical space and lab time. Overall factor rho/c is live and nonzero.

V5.citation: Visser, same local copy, p.4, section 2.1, equation (5)
V5.conditions: Background continuity; steady exterior specialization of the stated equation. No off-sheet source appears.

V6.citation: Visser, same local copy, p.4, section 2.1, equation (6)
V6.quoted: rho d v/dt = rho [partial_t v + (v dot nabla) v] = F
V6.conditions: Inviscid force accounting: pressure, Newtonian gravity and an external gradient force; their S9b counterparts are not supplied.

V7.citation: Visser, same local copy, p.4, section 2.1, equation (7)
V7.quoted: F = -nabla p - rho nabla phi - rho nabla Phi
V7.conditions: phi is Newtonian potential; Phi is externally imposed driving potential. No S9b force-law comparison is computed.

V7background.citation: Visser, same local copy, p.15, section 7, unnumbered background equations immediately preceding (53)
V7background.quoted: c = 1; v = sqrt(2GM/r); rho |v| proportional to 1/r^2; rho proportional to r^(-3/2); c^2 = dp/drho; p = p_infinity + c^2 rho; p-p_infinity proportional to c^2 r^(-3/2)
V7background.conditions: c is position independent. For constant rho and c with that velocity, the paper says: this assignment is incompatible with the continuity equation. Its displayed condition is nabla dot (rho v) != 0. Density-law normalizations remain unspecified. Neither density law is substituted into S9b's exchange.

V53.citation: Visser, same local copy, p.15, section 7, equation (53)
V53.quoted: ds^2 proportional to r^(-3/2) [-dt^2 + (dr +/- sqrt(2GM/r) dt)^2 + r^2(dtheta^2 + sin^2 theta dphi^2)]
V53.conditions: Both signs retained. The positive cross-term is the black-hole patch and the negative cross-term the white-hole patch. The proportionality constant is unspecified and printed separately.

V54.citation: Visser, same local copy, p.16, section 8, equation (54)
V54.conditions: Incompressible, spherically symmetric fluid. rho is position independent; the barotropic assumption makes pressure and c position independent. Continuity gives v proportional to 1/r^2. For the bubble realization use the exterior of the bubble and the incompressible approximation.

V55.citation: Visser, same local copy, p.16, section 8, equation (55)
V55.quoted: ds^2 = -c^2 dt^2 + (dr +/- c r_0^2/r^2 dt)^2 + r^2(dtheta^2 + sin^2 theta dphi^2)
V55.conditions: Both signs retained. The paper omits an overall position-independent factor; the underlying factor from (4) is rho/c, constant for this background.

V85.citation: Visser, same local copy, p.23, section 10, equation (85)
V85.conditions: rho/c removed from (4). This is the covariant metric, not the eikonal equation.

V86.citation: Visser, same local copy, p.23, section 10, equation (86)
V86.quoted: h^{mu nu} partial_mu varphi partial_nu varphi = 0
V86.conditions: Leading eikonal order; amplitude variations neglected. The inverse of (85) contracts the phase covector.

V87.citation: Visser, same local copy, p.23, section 10, equation (87)
V87.quoted: h_{mu nu} (dx^mu/dt)(dx^nu/dt) = 0 <=> -(c^2-v_0^2) - 2 v_0^i dx^i/dt + (dx^i/dt)(dx^i/dt) = 0 <=> ||dx/dt - v_0|| = c
V87.conditions: Norm is that of the flat physical spatial metric. This is a ray condition, not a material force equation.
